faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a truck driver in Perth?
faqs.a: Under the Road Transport and Distribution Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a full-time Transport Worker Grade 1 is $26.87 per hour from 1 July 2026. Higher grades pay more, up to $31.55 for Grade 10. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.59 per hour for Grade 1.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to truck driver pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the award are paid the ordinary hourly rate plus a 25% loading for each ordinary hour worked. This loading is not paid during overtime; instead, overtime rates apply plus a 10% of the minimum hourly rate. The casual loading is included in the rate you see in pay guides, so when using a calculator, enter the base rate without loading and check the casual loading option.

faqs.q: How do I calculate take-home pay from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Start with your hourly rate (e.g., $26.87). Multiply by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks to get annual gross pay ($53,087). Subtract tax using the 2026-27 resident tax scale (tax-free threshold up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, etc.) and the Medicare levy (2% of taxable income). Superannuation of 12% is paid on top by your employer, not deducted from your pay. Use our take-home pay tool for a detailed estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Truck Driver Salary Perth: Understanding Minimum Rates and Take-Home Pay

If you are looking for a **truck driver salary Perth** figure, the starting point is the Road Transport and Distribution Award 2020, which sets minimum pay rates for transport workers across Australia, including Perth. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, and how tax and superannuation affect your take-home amount.

### Minimum Hourly Rates Under the Award

The Fair Work Commission’s Road Transport and Distribution Award 2020 lists minimum hourly rates for full-time employees. From 1 July 2026, the rates are:

- Transport Worker Grade 1: $26.87 per hour
- Transport Worker Grade 2: $27.51
- Transport Worker Grade 3: $27.83
- Transport Worker Grade 4: $28.32
- Transport Worker Grade 5: $28.67
- Transport Worker Grade 6: $29.00
- Transport Worker Grade 7: $29.42
- Transport Worker Grade 8: $30.28
- Transport Worker Grade 9: $30.78
- Transport Worker Grade 10: $31.55

These rates apply nationally, so a **truck driver salary Perth** will be at least these amounts depending on the classification. The award also covers distribution facility employees with similar rates.

### Converting Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, the award defines ordinary hours as an average of 38 per week. So for a Grade 1 driver:

$26.87 × 38 × 52 = $53,087.12 per year

This is the gross annual salary before tax and before superannuation. The same calculation works for any hourly rate. If you work part-time, use your agreed weekly hours. For casuals, the rate already includes the 25% loading, so you would use the loaded rate in the formula.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

To find your fortnightly pay, multiply the weekly amount by 2:

- Weekly: $26.87 × 38 = $1,021.06
- Fortnightly: $1,021.06 × 2 = $2,042.12

These are gross figures. Your employer may pay weekly or fortnightly, but the annual total remains the same.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on the ordinary hourly rate. For Grade 1, that means $26.87 + 25% = $33.59 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), enter the base rate (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator adds the 25% automatically.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a Grade 1 driver earning $53,087, the employer contributes an extra $6,370.44 per year into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026-27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income above that is taxed at:

- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% on taxable income (with reductions for low-income earners). For a Grade 1 driver earning $53,087, the estimated tax is about $7,597 and Medicare $1,062, leaving a take-home of around $44,428 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a precise calculation.

### How the National Minimum Wage Compares

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates for truck drivers are higher, starting at $26.87. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides confirm that award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026, which is reflected in the rates above.

### Allowances and Other Payments

Truck drivers may receive allowances for things like meal breaks, overnight travel, or special duties. These are paid on top of the hourly rate and are taxable. The Australian Taxation Office requires you to declare all allowances as income. Some allowances are paid for all purposes, meaning they are included when calculating overtime and penalty rates.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page lets you enter any base hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Remember to select the correct employment type: full-time (38 hours), part-time (your agreed hours), or casual (with the 25% loading checkbox). The calculator assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% on ordinary earnings, and tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold.

### Summary for Perth Drivers

A **truck driver salary Perth** starts at $26.87 per hour for a Grade 1 transport worker. Annual gross pay is approximately $53,087, with super of $6,370 added on top. After tax and Medicare, take-home is around $44,428. Higher grades and casual employment increase these figures. Always check your classification under the award and use our [reference tables](/data) for the latest rates.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
